rows.notes: Exactly the sticky/split user examples plus three real ledger rows. Demo only, not a full encoding.
Cheats by pre-aggregating. Useful as a lower bound, not a fair codec.
Pre-aggregate for the three agent tasks. Fewest tokens, not a fair raw encoding.
Lossy. OCR quality will drop.
Vision tokens dominate if the strip is tall.
What the agent should get from API tools: balances, monthly series, category spend, subs, forecast window. Not a raw ledger.

GROUP BY month, category. Amounts are integer cents (divide by 100 for euros). Signed: +income -expense. discretionary=restaurants,entertainment,coffee,shopping,travel,gifts. Enough for reports/optimize/forecasts.
Inverted index: category -> cents list in date order, month marks. Reversible amounts+timing, names dropped.
Category-major RLE amounts (user style). Drops dates — forecasts need dsl_cat_month.
Monthly templates M+salary;R-rent;I-ins;G;N plus exception daypack list.
Category then merchant groups; D=days since 2025-01-01; V=cents; default eur/main. Token winner.
Merchant groups; first date is days since 2025-01-01, later rows are day deltas; cents.
Monthly+day packed freq-ranked 1-2 char merchant codes, cents, sparse account/ccy flags.
User sticky/split examples, then the winning group_cat_name_daynum ledger.
Category-major monthly inverted index with RLE. Best task-complete DSL.
freq_daypack with cents in signed base62. Legend still English; amounts need the alphabet.
Same monthly/day/cents packing but full merchant names — no codebook.
Category then merchant groups; YYMMDD + cents; default eur/main. Human-readable grouped win.
Group by merchant name (50 unique); category on the header; YYMMDD cents rows.
Sort by category, RLE block headers, delta-days, freq codes, cents.
Fair-enough for the three tasks: YYMMDD cents cat-code. Drops merchant names.
Monthly YYMM groups + 1-char CJK names/cats + cents. Full ledger (ccy/account flags). Best language attack.
Monthly buckets + dict_ids + cents; sparse account/ccy; spaces kept.
Same compact monthly layout but Hangul 1-syllable labels instead of CJK.
Template extraction: salary/rent/netflix/gym cron + exception ledger.
Monthly ideographs + 3-syllable Hangul-packed cents. Alphabet in legend.
Same compact monthly layout with 1-kanji/kata Japanese labels.
No JSON keys: parallel D/N/V integer streams plus sparse A/Y exception lists.
yaml_like monthly grouping combined with dict_ids: freq integer ids + cents + sparse Y/A.
Group by category so the label is written once; rows keep spaces (YYMMDD name cents).
gzip then base64. Fewer bytes, often more tokens.
Group by YYYY-MM; rows are DD name cents category. Reversible, spaces kept.
Structural cousin of line_natural: year-dropped months, cents, 1-char tags, spaces kept.
zlib then ascii85.
Glued YYMMDD+ideograph+cents+cat; omit default eur/main. Reversible via legend.
Monthly groups + 1-3 char name codes + cents + day-of-month. Full line items, reversible with legend.
Group by day (YYMMDD header) so the date is written once; rows keep spaces.
Minified JSON gzip+base64.
Flat lines: YYMMDD name cents category; list ccy/account only when not eur/main.
Readable 2-char Chinese names + monthly grouping + cents. Human-recoverable words, not 1-char codes.
Irreversible row hashes. Token-cheap, task-useless. Control for quality floor.
Monthly ideographs with CJK-digit amounts instead of ASCII cents (usually worse).
Keep spaces; YYMMDD dates + integer cents; full account/category words. Readable flat win.
Keep spaces; YYMMDD + cents + 1-letter account + 3-letter category + 1-letter ccy. Legend included.
Field reorder: cents, YYMMDD, name, ccy, account, category. Spaces kept.
Amount-first with a leading space so BPE sees ' -50' rather than start-of-line '-50'.
YYMMDD + cents + full words, but two ASCII spaces only between date and name (BPE boundary probe).
Field reorder: name first, YYMMDD last. Hurts BPE because names lose the leading-space merge.
Keep spaces and all fields; only compress ISO dates to YYMMDD.
YAML-ish nested months. Extra punctuation, usually worse.
Legend + integer ids + cents + day offsets. Usually the token winner among reversible codecs.
Pack numbers with CJK fullwidth digits + compact cats.
First date absolute, then day deltas. Amounts in cents.
Keep spaces and ISO dates; amounts as integer cents.
3-syllable base-80 Hangul packing of cents+121390. Alphabet in legend. English names.
One human line: 2026-01-02 groceries -23.10 eur main food
Tiny DSL: dYYMMDD nName vCents yA aA cCAT
German labels. Compound nouns can be 1-2 tokens or many.
Cyrillic labels.
Column-wise arrays. Helps models scan one field.
Full German ledger (merchants+cats+accounts) plus English legend.
User example: before '-50eur heh' after '-50 eur heh'. Split sign/amount/currency/name.
One mnemonic CJK char per merchant/category/account; spaced ISO lines; English legend.
Same payload as spaced_yymmdd_cents but ASCII spaces replaced by NBSP U+00A0.
Same payload as spaced_yymmdd_cents but ASCII spaces replaced by thin space U+2009.
Token-oriented object notation: declared columns, then rows.
Arabic labels.
Remove every ASCII space from the natural line format.
English merchants; CJK digit amounts; 1-char CJK categories. Mixed script.
User example: before '-50eur hahah' after '-50eurhahah'. Amount glued to currency and name.
Full Russian ledger (merchants+cats+accounts) plus English legend.
Emoji standing in for categories.
Chinese category/merchant labels. CJK is often cheaper on o200k.
Japanese labels.
Pinyin (no tones) for every merchant/category/account. Latin script, often worse than hanzi.
Drop vowels from names/categories. Lossy-ish but often readable.
Hangul digits 영일이삼사오육칠팔구음쩜 for amounts; English names; 1-char Hangul cats.
Full Korean merchants/cats/accounts plus English legend.
Spaces -> _
Full Chinese 2-char merchants/cats/accounts. Beats category-only zh because names shrink.
Spaces -> /
Tab-separated, no header.
CSV with header. Strong baseline for tabular data.
Spaces -> tab.
Full Japanese merchants/cats/accounts plus English legend.
Every separator is two spaces.
Spaces -> comma (CSV-ish without quoting).
Spaces -> | which is often a single token.
Each field on its own line; blank line between records.
ROT13 on names/categories only; numbers stay intact.
Spaces -> · (U+00B7).
Spaces -> ASCII unit separator 0x1f.
Spaces -> ▁ (U+2581) used by SentencePiece.
Minified JSON with default separators.
Base64 of the natural ledger. Usually expands tokens.
Hex of the natural ledger. Very expensive.
XOR with repeating key then hex. Opaque to models.
Indented JSON. Wasteful control, not an optimization.
